sec: The mechanism of ascites: the NO → retention chain · p1006

items.q: The mechanism chain begins with nitric oxide (NO) causing:
items.exp: Mechanism: nitric oxide (NO) → splanchnic vasodilation. (Book p1006)

items.q: Match the systems stimulated by ↓ effective intravascular volume — 1) Hormonal 2) Neural 3) Renin–angiotensin … A) RAAS B) Sympathetic nervous system (SNS) C) ADH
items.exp: ↓ effective intravascular volume stimulates ADH, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) and RAAS. (Book p1006)

items.q: ‘The fall in effective intravascular volume in the cirrhotic cascade is caused by splanchnic vasoconstriction.’
opts: False — it follows splanchnic vasodilation by NO
False — the volume falls before any vascular change
True, but only after RAAS activation
items.exp: Chain: NO → splanchnic vasodilation → ↓ effective intravascular volume → ADH/SNS/RAAS stimulation → ↑ salt + H₂O retention → ascites. (Book p1006)

items.q: All but one of the following are the three printed downstream states of ascites . The odd one out is:
items.exp: The ascites arrow branches to refractory ascites, hyponatremia and hepatorenal syndrome (HRS); encephalopathy is not in this p1006 branch. (Book p1006)

items.q: A cirrhotic with tense ascites has serum Na⁺ 124 mmol/L and a creatinine that has risen from 1.1 to 1.9 mg/dL over a week. Two of the three downstream states are present. Which pair?
items.exp: Na⁺ 124 = hyponatremia; the rising creatinine with ascites = the hepatorenal syndrome arm of the p1006 branch. (Book p1006)

items.q: In the pathophysiologic cascade of chronic liver disease, persistent renal retention of sodium and water directly manifests as:
items.exp: Increased salt and water retention directly produces peritoneal ascites. (Book p1006)
